concept.name: Fill model
concept.definition: A rule set that determines whether, when, at what price, and in what quantity a simulated order executes.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Evaluate the order type against eligible post-order market data, enforce price conditions, and emit full, partial, or no fill with a timestamp.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A buy limit at 100 fills 40 shares when a later trade prints 99.95 with only 40 shares allowed by the volume cap.

citations.source: QuantConnect LEAN documentation, Trade Fill Models
